title: Affine diagonal conormal coordinates and normalization formula
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], let $C$ be its diagonal conormal [def-sc-diagonal-conormal], and let $U\subset X$, $V\subset S$ be affine opens with $U\subset f^{-1}V$. Put $A=\Gamma(X,U)$ and $R=\Gamma(S,V)$ with the induced ring map. There exists an $A$-linear equivalence $e:\Omega_{A/R}\to\Gamma(U,C)$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] such that for every relative derivation $D:\mathcal O_X\to C$ normalized as in [lem-sc-diagonal-conormal-derivation-exists], $e(\mathrm da)=D(a)$ for every $a\in A$. The equivalence is independent of the choice of normalized derivation and does not involve the sheaf $\Omega_{X/S}$.

proof.text: The open U ×_V U of X ×_S X is Spec(A ⊗_R A), and its diagonal inverse image is U. On this chart the diagonal is the closed immersion corresponding to multiplication, whose kernel is I. Restriction of the actual sheaf-module kernel in the definition of diagonalConormal is the ideal sheaf of this closed immersion: restriction preserves kernels and restricts the diagonal pushforward to that of the restricted diagonal. Tensor pullback commutes with these restrictions by the canonical base-change isomorphisms. Their adjunction units are compatible because they are mates of the restriction isomorphisms.

Apply the affine conormal sections theorem to the restricted closed diagonal, identifying conormal sections with I/I² and the ideal-section class map with the tensor-pullback unit. This is linear over A via the multiplication quotient. Mathlib identifies KaehlerDifferential R A with this cotangent quotient, by the ring-level diagonal ideal theorem. Reverse the canonical identification to obtain e.

For a ∈ A, the section 1 ⊗ a − a ⊗ 1 belongs to I. Take its corresponding actual kernel section on the ambient affine open. The two projections pull a back to a ⊗ 1 and 1 ⊗ a respectively. The class-map formula and normalization of D give e of its cotangent class equal to D(a), after restriction to U. KaehlerDifferential.D_apply identifies this class with da. The construction of e does not use D, so the formula holds for every normalized D.

The diagonal conormal sheaf on an affine open is the multiplication ideal modulo its square, with normalized derivation sending a to the class of 1 tensor a minus a tensor 1
